reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Directed Hamiltonian Cycle = {<G> | G is a directed graph with a cycle that follows the edge directions and visits every node exactly once}
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: Directed Hamiltonian Cycle is the problem of determining whether a directed graph has a Hamiltonian cycle: a cycle that follows the edge directions, visits every vertex exactly once, and returns to the vertex it started from.
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether G has a Hamiltonian cycle
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: {q0,...,qn,q0} | Hamiltonian cycle: every node exactly once, each (qi,qi+1) in E, ends by repeating q0 Example: {2,1,3,5,4,2}

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Hamiltonian Cycle = {<G> | G is an undirected graph with a cycle that visits every node exactly once}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: Hamiltonian Cycle is the problem of determining whether an undirected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle: a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once and returns to the vertex it started from.
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether G has a Hamiltonian cycle
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Format: {(N,E) | N is set, E subset N unorderedcross N} Example: ({1,2,3,4,5},{{2,1},{1,3},{2,3},{3,5},{2,4},{4,5}})
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: {q0,...,qn} | Hamiltonian cycle: every node exactly once, each (qi,qi+1) and (qn,q0) in E Example: {1,2,4,5,3}
